answer: Every agent must anchor its key inside a physical enclave whose factory-signed summit cannot be virtualized or cloned. To register the $n$-th simultaneous identity on the same summit, the enclave's internal counter forces the operator to lock $2^n$ ETH into a time-locked glacier before the ledger grants a routing zenith. A genuine newcomer with one machine locks 2 ETH into its glacier for a full zenith, whereas an attacker cramming $n$ fake identities onto existing hardware pays $2^{n+1}-2$ ETH in frozen capital or must purchase $n$ separate physical machines.
